A.interpretation: Regime A — Class-3 diagnosis: IRREDUCIBLE CEILING PROBLEM. The train-derived oracle achieves a per-class ceiling accuracy of 0.1037 on class 3, and the frozen kNN baseline scores 0.0807, giving a gap of -0.0231 (kNN minus ceiling). The gap of -0.0231 is within the ±5 pp threshold, so the kNN baseline is essentially at its own per-class ceiling for class 3. The low accuracy (0.0807) is explained by the ceiling itself being low — a data and annotation-noise limitation, not a decoding failure. Mean entropy of class-3-modal texts is 1.6808 bits, higher than class-4-modal texts (1.6585 bits), confirming that class-3 texts carry more within-text rater disagreement and their low ceiling is structurally determined by annotation noise. 92.2% of class-3 misclassifications land within ±1 (predicted 2 or 4), consistent with genuine adjacent-class ambiguity rather than systematic error. Conclusion: improving class-3 accuracy requires more consistent annotations or a richer feature space — it is not fixable by changing the decoding rule alone. Class-2 verdict: IRREDUCIBLE CEILING PROBLEM (kNN=0.4808, ceiling=0.4679, gap=+0.0128).

B.interpretation: Regime B — Class-3 diagnosis: IRREDUCIBLE CEILING PROBLEM. In Regime B every test text is unseen at training time (n_fallback = 1797/1797, confirmed in ceiling_summary.json), so the train-derived oracle degenerates to always predicting the global-prior mode (rating 4). Its per-class ceiling for class 3 is therefore 0.0000 — not because class 3 is especially hard, but because the oracle has no text-specific information at all. The kNN baseline scores 0.0650 on class 3 by using embedding similarity to seen training texts, which is better than the degenerate oracle, confirming semantic generalisation. The per-class ceiling for Regime B is not an informative upper bound by class; the informative comparison is Regime A, where the ceiling is 0.1037 and the gap is only −0.0231 (IRREDUCIBLE). Mean entropy of class-3-modal texts in the Regime B training split: 1.6733 bits. 96.5% of class-3 errors fall within ±1 of the true rating (predicted 2 or 4), consistent with adjacent-class ambiguity rather than systematic error. Conclusion: class-3 low accuracy is an irreducible consequence of annotation noise, not fixable by changing the decoding rule. Class-2 verdict: IRREDUCIBLE CEILING PROBLEM (kNN=0.3859, oracle ceiling=0.0000 — degenerate for same reason).
